solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cuddly character in game — forward needing support

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
forward in the sense of cheeky, impudent: pert
to bear is to support or hold up

explanation.surface: A rugby forward who needs propping up by a teammate, with 'cuddly character' hinting at a teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is a standard abbreviation; 'forward' is the adjective meaning saucy, not the rugby position the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon bear in checked trousers from the Daily Express strip is a much-loved children's character, and a bear is cuddly.

clue.text: Finishes off eclair, gateau, scones and rock cake

indicators.note: the finishes of these words are their final letters

explanation.surface: Someone polishing off a plate of assorted pastries and cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock cake' reads as one item, but only 'rock' gives a letter and 'cake' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard dry biscuit-like bake, often given to teething babies, is loosely a kind of cake.

clue.text: Average about one or two

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for average goes round the numeral

parts.note: par is the average or normal standard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An estimate of 'about one or two', vague and average.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple or brace is a set of two.

clue.text: Toy animal lulling her, so woolly

parts.note: rocking a baby lulls it

indicators.note: woolly means muddled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A toy lamb or sheep soothing a woman, being soft and woolly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden steed on curved rockers that a child rides is a classic toy animal.

clue.text: Head's embracing runs and stretches between lessons

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the head's word wraps around the letter

parts.note: beak is schoolboy slang for headmaster, so 'Head's' gives BEAK'S
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A headteacher hugging the playground runners at break.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is old British slang for a headmaster or magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: School has short recesses between classes, periods of time out between lessons.

clue.text: Their Acts are authorised!

parts.note: the book of the Bible called the Acts of these men appears in the Authorised Version

explanation.surface: A group whose performances have been officially approved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised Version is the King James Bible, which includes the book of Acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's twelve disciples sent out to preach are the subject of the New Testament book of Acts.

clue.text: Twisted plans for some emails

indicators.note: twisted round so the word for the plans is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Devious schemes carried out by email, as fraudsters might.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited bulk messages are known by this name, so it describes some of the emails anyone receives.

clue.text: Fussy item

definitions.meaning: a detail or single point, as in 'in every respect'

explanation.definitionFit: A choosy person is fastidious; as a noun the word means a detail or individual point, an item.

clue.text: End of Prom — time to interrupt one composer or another

indicators.note: the end of the word means its final letter
interrupting means breaking into the number word

parts.note: taken as the word itself
another composer: Verdi, the Italian opera writer

explanation.surface: A Proms concert finishing with one composer's work cut short by time, or another's.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a BBC summer season of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian who wrote the early opera Orfeo was a renowned composer.

clue.text: Now listening to Radio 4, say, with it

definitions.meaning: a radio that has just been turned on, so you are listening

explanation.surface: Someone tuning in to BBC Radio 4 and feeling thoroughly modern.
explanation.definitionFit: A set turned on is one you are listening to; colloquially the phrase also means alert and fashionable, like 'with it'.

clue.text: Irish working club

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A golf club or social club in Ireland that is still in business.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a metal-headed stick of this kind is one of the clubs in a player's bag.

clue.text: What you take when the disc finishes — unofficially

definitions.text: What you take when the disc finishes
definitions.meaning: you lift the needle from the vinyl when the song ends
said in confidence, not for publication

explanation.definitionFit: A remark made without attribution is not for publication, hence unofficial; literally the stylus comes away from the vinyl.

clue.text: Instant coffee; it is free in this point of purchase

parts.note: a tick is an instant, as in 'just a tick'

indicators.note: set free, so the letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A sales booth giving away instant coffee to customers buying from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective for the coffee but is a noun for TICK; 'free' rearranges COFFEE IT into ETOFFICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking booth at a station or theatre is where tickets are bought, the place of purchase.

clue.text: Liver and lime mixed with cold pasta

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A recipe combining liver and lime with chilled pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Very thin Italian noodles, finer than spaghetti, are a type of pasta.

clue.text: Moonlight escape around river transformed into a brief liaison

indicators.note: around means the escape word goes round the letter

parts.note: a moonlight flit is a secret night-time departure to avoid paying debts

indicators.note: transformed means the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Eloping by moonlight beside a river, a romance turning into a short affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'moonlight flit' is British slang for leaving secretly, often to dodge rent. 'transformed' reworks INTO A as ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful romance without serious intent is a dalliance, a brief liaison.

clue.text: Deadication?

parts.note: a punning blend of 'dead' and 'dedication': words dedicated to someone who has died

explanation.surface: A misspelt 'dedication' with a ghoulish twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech of praise given at a funeral honours the deceased, a tribute dedicated to the dead.

clue.text: Match on TV — it's experimental

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
the tube is slang for television

explanation.surface: A cricket Test broadcast on television in a novel way.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a cricket international between countries, a sense less familiar outside cricketing nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, as in a test-tube baby, the phrase means produced by laboratory experiment.

clue.text: Dealer that's often associated with speed

definitions.meaning: a speed ... is a fast driver or runner

explanation.surface: A drug dealer known for supplying amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' suggests the drug, but the phrase 'speed merchant' means a very fast person.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is a dealer in goods; the word pairs with speed in the idiom for a fast mover.

clue.text: Monkey hurt, doctor ready

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: An injured monkey with a doctor standing by.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate with a long tail, a species of monkey.

clue.text: Compensation for artist in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word for the artist runs backwards

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: Payment made to a painter who has gone away on a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given in return for effort or service is a recompense, a form of compensation.

clue.text: Capital left in the midst of crazed behaviour

indicators.note: in the midst of means placed inside the word for crazed behaviour

parts.note: mania is frenzied, crazed behaviour

explanation.surface: A capital city where everyone left amid scenes of madness.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of the Philippines is that country's capital.

clue.text: Greeks and Romans in The Oaks and Derby, say

definitions.meaning: two of the five English flat-racing Classics run each year

explanation.surface: Ancient Greek and Roman runners competing at English racecourses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks and the Derby are famous English horse races run at Epsom, two of the five 'Classics'.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeks and Romans were peoples of the classical world; the Oaks and Derby are among England's prestige flat races known as the Classics.

clue.text: No parking during month having rolled up in old European capital

indicators.note: in a down clue rolling up means reading from the bottom upwards
no parking means the parking letter is taken away

parts.note: April is a month

explanation.surface: A parking ban for a month in an old European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means money: the former currency of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Italy before the euro was old European capital in the sense of money.

clue.text: King once called for a joint

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née means formerly called, used of a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A former king who once summoned someone to a pub or to share a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge in the middle of the leg is a body joint.

clue.text: City beside which this person had settled

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the setter refers to themself as 'this person', so I'D (I had)

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a city beside which they had made their home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust that has come to rest has settled; something put down and lying in place is likewise at rest.

clue.text: Poor Naomi can go back inside for Welsh stories

indicators.note: placed inside means the following letters go into the shuffled name
poor here means badly arranged, so the letters of the name are shuffled

parts.note: a bin is a can, as in a rubbish bin

indicators.note: going back means the little word is read the other way round

explanation.surface: A struggling Naomi being able to retreat indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for Naomi but signals rearranging her name; 'can' is the noun, a rubbish bin, not the verb. The Mabinogion is the classic medieval Welsh tale collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval collection of Welsh prose tales is known by this title, a set of stories.

clue.text: Europeans with no head for travellers' accommodation

indicators.note: a word without its head has lost its first letter

parts.note: Finns are people from Finland, Europeans

explanation.surface: European tourists with nowhere to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelries offering rooms and food along a route have long served as lodging for those on the road.

clue.text: Dish taken aside in mess

indicators.note: being in a mess means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A plate of food carried aside in the officers' mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' suggests a military dining room, but here it signals jumbling the letters of TAKEN ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic restaurant main course of beef in a flambéed sauce, served as a dish.
